metrics.name: Resting heart rate and pulse
metrics.definition: Heart or pulse rate, in beats per minute, while the person is at rest. The value depends on how and when it is taken, so each source below states its method.

sources.title: Quer et al. 2020, Fitbit wearable cohort (92,457 US adults), daily resting heart rate
Fitbit daily resting heart rate by sex, 92,457 US adults, 2016-2018 (Quer et al. 2020, distribution digitised from Fig 2)

metrics.methodological_warning: Never pool clinic seated pulse (NHANES 30s count) with ambulatory/nocturnal wearable resting heart rate (Fitbit). A 7 bpm physiological offset exists between seated clinic exam counts and waking basal wearable rates.

metrics.name: Blood pressure (systolic and diastolic)
metrics.definition: Auscultatory systolic and diastolic blood pressure in mmHg measured by physician examiners using a calibrated mercury sphygmomanometer after 5 minutes of seated rest.
metrics.methodological_warning: Auscultatory clinic blood pressure reflects daytime resting arterial pressure and incorporates situational alerting (white-coat) effects. Continuous cuffless wearable estimates (optical pulse transit time, PTT) and ambulatory 24-hour recordings (ABPM) are distinct physiological measurement paradigms and must not be pooled with clinic auscultation.

metrics.name: Height, body mass, and BMI
metrics.definition: Anthropometric body dimensions (Body Mass Index in kg/m^2 and mid-upper arm circumference in cm) measured by trained examiners following standardized CDC health examination protocols.
metrics.methodological_warning: Wrist and arm circumference directly govern sensor optical coupling and motion artifact vulnerability. Subcutaneous adipose tissue (BMI) alters optical photon path lengths.

metrics.name: Skin tone (Monk, Fitzpatrick, individual typology angle)
metrics.definition: How light or dark a person's skin is, recorded on one of three kinds of scale. Fitzpatrick skin type (I to VI) classifies people by their response to sun exposure, in terms of tanning and burning. The Monk Skin Tone scale is a 10-shade scale of colour swatches that a person or an observer matches to the skin. The individual typology angle (ITA) is a number in degrees calculated from CIELAB lightness (L*) and yellow-blue (b*) readings taken with a colorimeter or spectrophotometer.

metrics.methodological_warning: Never pool self-reported Fitzpatrick phototypes with dermatologist photograph ratings or instrument ITA. Never apply hierarchical shrinkage across skin tones (ADR-006: anti-whitewashing invariant).

metrics.name: Sleep duration
metrics.methodological_warning: Self-reported questionnaire sleep hours and wearable actigraphy/PPG sleep duration systematically diverge. Questionnaires reflect time in bed; sensors reflect detected immobility.

metrics.name: Sleep stage proportions
metrics.methodological_warning: Never pool gold-standard in-lab polysomnography (PSG 30s EEG epochs) with wearable surrogate stage heuristics. Wake after sleep onset (WASO) is systematically underestimated by optical/motion sensors.
